accepted.s: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of which Mughal emperor?
accepted.x: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of Shah Jahan.
accepted.tq: Use the direct person–relationship link.

accepted.s: Dara Shikoh was associated with which Sufi order?
accepted.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order and was associated with Miyan Mir and Muhibullah Shah.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related Sufi orders by their associated personalities.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sirr-i-Akbar — Persian translation of the Upanishads
Majma-ul-Bahrain — Persian translation of the Ramayana
Razmnama — Persian translation of the Atharvaveda
Lilavati — Persian translation of the Rajatarangini
accepted.x: Sirr-i-Akbar, meaning ‘The Great Secret’, was Dara Shikoh’s Persian translation of the Upanishads.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure work–subject pair and eliminate swapped titles.

accepted.s: Who served as Dara Shikoh’s physician?
accepted.x: Bernier was Dara Shikoh’s physician, whereas Manucci served in his artillery.
accepted.tq: Separate the two European associates by their respective roles.

accepted.s: Manucci was associated with Dara Shikoh as his
o: spiritual guide in the Qadiri order
accepted.x: Manucci served in Dara Shikoh’s artillery; Bernier was his physician.
accepted.tq: Test a role distinction between two closely associated persons.

accepted.s: The Naqshbandi order is traditionally associated with which founder?
accepted.x: The Naqshbandi order was founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband and came to India with Babur.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–order association directly.
accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal religious orientation of the Naqshbandi order mentioned in the context of medieval India?
o: Strict adherence to Islamic law or Sharia
accepted.x: The Naqshbandi order stressed strict adherence to Islamic law, or Sharia.
accepted.tq: Identify the doctrine from its defining orientation rather than its name.
accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known by which title?
accepted.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani.
accepted.tq: Match the religious personality with the exact title.
accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi criticised which of the following policies or doctrines associated with Akbar?
1. Sulh-i-kul
2. Din-i-Ilahi
3. Rajput partnership
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi. The material does not identify him as criticising Akbar’s Rajput partnership.

accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi propounded which doctrine in opposition to Wahdat-ul-Wujud?
accepted.x: Sirhindi propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud, or Unity of Appearance, against Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar-sounding mystical doctrines.
accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following scholars were later associated with the Naqshbandi tradition?
1. Shah Waliullah
2. Shah Abdul Aziz
3. Faizi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Shah Waliullah and Shah Abdul Aziz were later Naqshbandi scholars. Faizi was associated with the translation of Lilavati, not listed as a later Naqshbandi scholar here.
accepted.tq: Separate later order scholars from court translators.
accepted.sec: Orthodox reaction - Naqshbandi order and its leaders [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Order)
a. Qadiri
b. Naqshbandi

List-II (Feature)
i. Founded by Baha-ud-din Naqshband
ii. Associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani

accepted.s: Akbar’s translation department at Fatehpur Sikri was known as

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Lilavati was translated by Faizi. Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi was associated with the translation of Rajatarangini.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped translator by checking the less familiar pair.

accepted.s: Razmnama was the Persian title given to the translation of which Sanskrit work?
accepted.x: The Persian translation of the Mahabharata was known as Razmnama.
accepted.tq: Test the exact translated-title association.

accepted.s:
Who among the following were associated with the Persian translation of the Mahabharata known as Razmnama?
1. Badauni
2. Naqib Khan
3. Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Badauni and Naqib Khan, along with others, were associated with the translation of the Mahabharata as Razmnama. Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda.
accepted.tq: Separate translators of different Sanskrit works.
accepted.sec: Translation bureau - Maktab Khana and translated texts [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who translated the Ramayana into Persian in Akbar’s translation bureau?
accepted.x: Badauni was associated with the Persian translation of the Ramayana.
accepted.tq: Use the direct text–translator association.

accepted.s: The Persian translation of the Atharvaveda was associated with
accepted.x: Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda into Persian.
accepted.tq: Distinguish individual translators by the Sanskrit work assigned to them.
accepted.sec: Translation bureau - Maktab Khana and translated texts [GROUP-II]

accepted.x: Faizi translated Lilavati, a mathematical work, into Persian.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following works according to the translators associated with them, beginning with the work translated by Badauni and ending with the work translated by Faizi:
A. Lilavati
B. Ramayana
C. Atharvaveda
D. Rajatarangini
accepted.x: Badauni translated the Ramayana, Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi the Atharvaveda, Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi the Rajatarangini, and Faizi Lilavati.

accepted.s: Which development most directly helped transform the Mughal state from a conquest state into a durable empire?
o: The withdrawal from Rajput affairs and restriction of Hindu participation
The exclusive use of Persian in local administration
The abolition of the mansabdari system
The combination of Sulh-i-Kul with partnership with the Rajputs
accepted.x: Sulh-i-Kul and the Rajput partnership broadened support and helped turn the conquest state into a durable empire.
accepted.tq: Link the stated policy with its institutional and political consequence.

accepted.s: Akbar abolished jizya in which year?
accepted.x: Akbar abolished jizya in 1564.
accepted.tq: Separate the abolition year from the later reimposition year.

accepted.s: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in
accepted.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679, reversing Akbar’s policy of abolition.
accepted.tq: Use the paired date comparison to avoid reversing abolition and reimposition.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Din-i-Ilahi has been debated as either a new religion or a discipleship order.
2. Only a handful of people joined it.
3. It continued as a major institution after Akbar’s death.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The first two statements are correct. Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution after his reign.
accepted.tq: Reject the overstatement about the size and continuity of a short-lived institution.

accepted.s: The core components of Mughal governance that remained significant for about 150 years were
o: Maktab Khana, Ibadat Khana and Razmnama
accepted.x: Mansabdari, jagirdari and Zabti formed the core of Mughal governance for about 150 years.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative cluster rather than a religious or cultural cluster.

accepted.s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs
accepted.x: The jagirdari crisis arose because too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs, which increased pressure on the peasantry.
accepted.tq: Translate the economic consequence into an administrative scenario.

accepted.s: Which ruler of Golconda maintained friendly relations with Akbar and received Masud Beg with gifts?
accepted.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda maintained friendly relations with Akbar, who sent Masud Beg with gifts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Golconda ruler associated with Akbar from later court officials.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the religious policy of Abul Hasan Tana Shah?
o: He followed religious tolerance and appointed Madanna and Akkanna to high office.
He abolished all high offices held by non-Muslims.
He founded the Naqshbandi order in Golconda.
accepted.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah followed religious tolerance and appointed Madanna and Akkanna to high office.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–policy–appointment combination.

accepted.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was related to Madanna and Akkanna as their
accepted.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.
accepted.tq: Test the precise kinship relationship rather than a general association.

accepted.s: Sirhind Fateh Diwas, observed from 12 to 14 May, commemorates
o: The foundation of the Khalsa in 1699
Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind in 1710
accepted.x: Sirhind Fateh Diwas commemorates Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind in 1710 and is observed from 12 to 14 May.
accepted.tq: Match the observance with its event, year and date range.

accepted.s: Guru Tegh Bahadur’s martyrdom is observed as Shaheedi Divas on
accepted.x: Shaheedi Divas commemorating Guru Tegh Bahadur’s martyrdom is observed on 24 November.
accepted.tq: Distinguish commemorative dates that occur close to other Sikh observances.

accepted.s: Baisakhi is recalled as the foundation day of the Khalsa, associated with the date
accepted.x: Baisakhi is recalled as the foundation day of the Khalsa on 13 April 1699.
accepted.tq: Separate the historical foundation date from the modern reporting date.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baisakhi — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
Baisakhi — foundation day of the Khalsa
Shaheedi Divas — martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sirhind Fateh Diwas — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
accepted.x: Baisakhi is associated with the foundation of the Khalsa, not Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind. The conquest is commemorated by Sirhind Fateh Diwas.
accepted.tq: Find the event–observance swap among related Sikh commemorations.
